claim: Rapid recovery of proteasome activity may contribute to intrinsic and acquired resistance to FDA-approved proteasome inhibitors.
source: Rapid recovery of proteasome activity may contribute to intrinsic and acquired resistance to FDA-approved proteasome inhibitors.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that represents a hypothesis or speculation about the clinical significance of proteasome activity recovery.

claim: The expression of proteasome genes in cells treated with sub-lethal concentrations of proteasome inhibitors is upregulated by the transcription factor Nrf1 (NFE2L1).
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that the expression of proteasome genes in cells treated with sub-lethal concentrations of proteasome inhibitors is upregulated by the transcription factor Nrf1 (NFE2L1), which is activated by a DDI2 protease.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to previous studies, as indicated by the phrase 'Previous studies have demonstrated'.

claim: Nrf1 is activated by a DDI2 protease.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that the expression of proteasome genes in cells treated with sub-lethal concentrations of proteasome inhibitors is upregulated by the transcription factor Nrf1 (NFE2L1), which is activated by a DDI2 protease.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to previous studies.

claim: The recovery of proteasome activity is DDI2-independent.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the recovery of proteasome activity is DDI2-independent and occurs before transcription of proteasomal genes is upregulated but requires protein translation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The recovery of proteasome activity occurs before transcription of proteasomal genes is upregulated.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the recovery of proteasome activity is DDI2-independent and occurs before transcription of proteasomal genes is upregulated but requires protein translation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The recovery of proteasome activity requires protein translation.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the recovery of proteasome activity is DDI2-independent and occurs before transcription of proteasomal genes is upregulated but requires protein translation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cycloheximide experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mammalian cells possess an additional DDI2 and transcription-independent pathway for the rapid recovery of proteasome activity after proteasome inhibition.
source: Thus, mammalian cells possess an additional DDI2 and transcription-independent pathway for the rapid recovery of proteasome activity after proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from the experimental data showing DDI2-independent recovery.

claim: Malignant cells are more dependent on proteasome function than non-transformed cells because they divide rapidly and produce abnormal proteins at a higher rate than normal cells.
source: Malignant cells are more dependent on proteasome function than non-transformed cells because they divide rapidly and produce abnormal proteins at a higher rate than normal cells (Deshaies, 2014; Kisselev et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Proteasome inhibitors bortezomib (Btz), carfilzomib (Cfz), and ixazomib are approved for the treatment of multiple myeloma (MM).
source: Proteasome inhibitors (PIs) bortezomib (Btz), carfilzomib (Cfz), and ixazomib are approved for the treatment of multiple myeloma (MM).
evidence: This is established knowledge about FDA-approved drugs.

claim: Bortezomib is approved for the treatment of mantle cell lymphoma (MCL).
source: Btz is also approved for the treatment of mantle cell lymphoma (MCL).
evidence: This is established knowledge about FDA-approved drug indications.

claim: MM cells are exquisitely sensitive to PIs because the production of immunoglobulins by these malignant plasma cells places an enormous load on the proteasome and other components of the protein quality control machinery.
source: MM cells are exquisitely sensitive to PIs because the production of immunoglobulins by these malignant plasma cells places an enormous load on the proteasome and other components of the protein quality control machinery (Cascio et al., 2008; Bianchi et al., 2009; Cenci et al., 2011; Shabaneh et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Bortezomib and carfilzomib are administered once or twice weekly as a subcutaneous (Btz) or intravenous bolus.
source: Clinically, Btz and Cfz are administered once or twice weekly as a subcutaneous (Btz) or intravenous bolus.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about drug administration.

claim: Bortezomib and carfilzomib cause rapid inhibition of proteasome activity in the patients' blood but are metabolized rapidly.
source: They cause rapid inhibition of proteasome activity in the patients' blood but are metabolized rapidly (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Within an hour after the administration, PIs concentrations in the blood drop below the levels needed to kill tumor cells in vitro.
source: Within an hour after the administration, PIs concentrations in the blood drop below the levels needed to kill tumor cells in vitro (Hamilton et al., 2005; Moreau et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Bortezomib has a very slow off-rate.
source: Although Btz has a very slow off-rate and Cfz is an irreversible inhibitor, proteasome activity recovers within 24 hr (Shabaneh et al., 2013; Hamilton et al., 2005; O'Connor et al., 2009; Weyburne et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the biochemical properties of bortezomib.

claim: Carfilzomib is an irreversible inhibitor.
source: Although Btz has a very slow off-rate and Cfz is an irreversible inhibitor, proteasome activity recovers within 24 hr (Shabaneh et al., 2013; Hamilton et al., 2005; O'Connor et al., 2009; Weyburne et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the biochemical properties of carfilzomib.

claim: Proteasome activity recovers within 24 hr after treatment with bortezomib or carfilzomib.
source: Although Btz has a very slow off-rate and Cfz is an irreversible inhibitor, proteasome activity recovers within 24 hr (Shabaneh et al., 2013; Hamilton et al., 2005; O'Connor et al., 2009; Weyburne et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activity recovery may explain discrepancies between robust activity against cell lines derived from various cancers, continuously treated with Btz, and a lack of clinical efficacy except in MM and MCL.
source: This activity recovery may explain discrepancies between robust activity against cell lines derived from various cancers, continuously treated with Btz (http://www.carcerrxgene.org/) (Shabaneh et al., 2013), and a lack of clinical efficacy except in MM and MCL.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the significance of activity recovery.

claim: Recovery of activity has recently been implicated in PI resistance in MM.
source: In addition, recovery of activity has recently been implicated in PI resistance in MM (Op et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to recent literature.

claim: In cells treated with PIs, a transcription factor Nrf1 (also known as TCF11, encoded by the NFE2L1 gene) upregulates the transcription of genes encoding all proteasome subunits.
source: In cells treated with PIs, a transcription factor Nrf1 (also known as TCF11, encoded by the NFE2L1 gene) upregulates the transcription of genes encoding all proteasome subunits (Steffen et al., 2010; Radhakrishnan et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: When the proteasome is fully functional, Nrf1 is constitutively degraded in a ubiquitin-dependent manner.
source: When the proteasome is fully functional, Nrf1 is constitutively degraded in a ubiquitin-dependent manner (Steffen et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: When the proteasome is partially inhibited, the ubiquitylated Nrf1 is recognized by DDI2 (DNA-Damage-Inducible I Homolog 2), a ubiquitin-dependent aspartic protease that activates Nrf1 by a site-specific cleavage.
source: When the proteasome is partially inhibited, the ubiquitylated Nrf1 is recognized by DDI2 (DNA-Damage-Inducible I Homolog 2), a ubiquitin-dependent aspartic protease that activates Nrf1 by a site-specific cleavage (Koizumi et al., 2016; Lehrbach and Ruvkun, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Knockdown of DDI2 blocks the PI-induced transcription of proteasome genes.
source: Although knockdown of DDI2 blocks the PI-induced transcription of proteasome genes (Koizumi et al., 2016; Lehrbach and Ruvkun, 2016), initial studies implicating DDI2 in the activation of Nrf1 did not determine whether DDI2/Nrf1-dependent transcription leads to the recovery of activity after clinically relevant pulse treatment with PIs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Initial studies implicating DDI2 in the activation of Nrf1 did not determine whether DDI2/Nrf1-dependent transcription leads to the recovery of activity after clinically relevant pulse treatment with PIs.
source: Although knockdown of DDI2 blocks the PI-induced transcription of proteasome genes (Koizumi et al., 2016; Lehrbach and Ruvkun, 2016), initial studies implicating DDI2 in the activation of Nrf1 did not determine whether DDI2/Nrf1-dependent transcription leads to the recovery of activity after clinically relevant pulse treatment with PIs.
evidence: This is an observation about gaps in previous literature.

claim: Proteasome activity recovered in the absence of DDI2.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that proteasome activity recovered in the absence of DDI2, and activity recovery preceded the upregulation of proteasome genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Activity recovery preceded the upregulation of proteasome genes.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that proteasome activity recovered in the absence of DDI2, and activity recovery preceded the upregulation of proteasome genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: This data demonstrates the existence of a novel, DDI2-independent pathway for the recovery of proteasome activity in PI-treated cells.
source: This data demonstrates the existence of a novel, DDI2-independent pathway for the recovery of proteasome activity in PI-treated cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from the experimental data.

claim: No differences in the recovery between wt and DDI2-KO clones were observed.
source: Surprisingly, no differences in the recovery between wt and DDI2-KO clones were observed (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Deletion of DDI2 did not affect recovery, despite inhibition of Btz-induced proteolytic activation of Nrf1.
source: Deletion of DDI2 did not affect recovery, despite inhibition of Btz-induced proteolytic activation of Nrf1 (Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: DDI2 activates Nrf1.
source: These findings confirm that DDI2 activates Nrf1, but indicate that it is not involved in the recovery of proteasome activity in Btz and Cfz-treated HAP1 and DDI2 KO cells.
evidence: This claim is confirmed by the experimental data in the study.

claim: DDI2 is not involved in the recovery of proteasome activity in Btz and Cfz-treated HAP1 and DDI2 KO cells.
source: These findings confirm that DDI2 activates Nrf1, but indicate that it is not involved in the recovery of proteasome activity in Btz and Cfz-treated HAP1 and DDI2 KO cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The recovery of proteasome activity after pulse treatment with sub-toxic concentrations of PIs is DDI2-independent.
source: Thus, the recovery of proteasome activity after pulse treatment with sub-toxic concentrations of PIs is DDI2-independent.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by experimental data from multiple cell lines.

claim: The recovery of activity started immediately after 1 hr pulse treatment and approached a plateau after 8 hr.
source: However, we found that the recovery of activity started immediately after 1 hr pulse treatment and approached a plateau after 8 hr (Figure 2a), but the first significant increase in the expression of proteasomal mRNAs occurred only 8 hr after the removal of the inhibitor (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The first significant increase in the expression of proteasomal mRNAs occurred only 8 hr after the removal of the inhibitor.
source: However, we found that the recovery of activity started immediately after 1 hr pulse treatment and approached a plateau after 8 hr (Figure 2a), but the first significant increase in the expression of proteasomal mRNAs occurred only 8 hr after the removal of the inhibitor (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The early recovery of the proteasome activity is not a transcriptional response.
source: These results suggest that the early recovery of the proteasome activity is not a transcriptional response.
evidence: This is inferred from the timing data showing activity recovery precedes mRNA upregulation.

claim: Except for the first hour, the recovery was completely blocked by CHX, independent of DDI2 expression status.
source: Except for the first hour, the recovery was completely blocked by CHX, independent of DDI2 expression status (Figure 3a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The recovery of proteasome activity involves protein synthesis.
source: Thus, the recovery of proteasome activity involves protein synthesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the cycloheximide blocking experiments.

claim: 90% of proteasomal mRNAs are ribosome or polysome bound in untreated cells.
source: We found that 90% of proteasomal mRNAs are ribosome or polysome bound in untreated cells (Figure 3b), and treatment with inhibitors did not increase this fraction (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from polysome profiling shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Treatment with inhibitors did not increase the fraction of proteasomal mRNAs that are ribosome or polysome bound.
source: We found that 90% of proteasomal mRNAs are ribosome or polysome bound in untreated cells (Figure 3b), and treatment with inhibitors did not increase this fraction (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The amount of proteasome mRNA in the polysomal fraction does not increase when proteasome is inhibited in MM1.S cells.
source: This result agrees with a published result that the amount of proteasome mRNA in the polysomal fraction does not increase when proteasome is inhibited in MM1.S cells (Wiita et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The biosynthesis of active new proteasomes immediately after treatment with sub-lethal concentrations of PIs appears to occur without upregulation of translation of mRNAs encoding proteasome subunits.
source: Thus, the biosynthesis of active new proteasomes immediately after treatment with sub-lethal concentrations of PIs appears to occur without upregulation of translation of mRNAs encoding proteasome subunits.
evidence: This is inferred from the polysome profiling data showing no increase in translation.

claim: In addition to Nrf1/DDI2 pathway, mammalian cells possess at least one additional pathway to restore proteasome activity after treatment with PIs.
source: The most important conclusion of this work is that, in addition to Nrf1/DDI2 pathway, mammalian cells possess at least one additional pathway to restore proteasome activity after treatment with PIs, and this DDI2-independent pathway is responsible for the rapid synthesis of new proteasomes immediately after treatment with PI.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study inferred from the experimental data.

claim: The DDI2-independent pathway is responsible for the rapid synthesis of new proteasomes immediately after treatment with PI.
source: The most important conclusion of this work is that, in addition to Nrf1/DDI2 pathway, mammalian cells possess at least one additional pathway to restore proteasome activity after treatment with PIs, and this DDI2-independent pathway is responsible for the rapid synthesis of new proteasomes immediately after treatment with PI.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing DDI2-independent recovery.

claim: Knockout of DDI2 reduced recovery of proteasome activity in multiple myeloma and NIH-3T3 cells pulse-treated with PIs by ~30%.
source: While this study was underway, two other laboratories found that knockout of DDI2 reduced recovery of proteasome activity in multiple myeloma and NIH-3T3 cells pulse-treated with PIs by ~30% (Chen et al., 2022; Northrop et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: Nrf1 knockdown did not completely block the recovery of proteasome activity in mouse embryonal fibroblasts.
source: Similarly, Nrf1 knockdown did not completely block the recovery of proteasome activity in mouse embryonal fibroblasts (Radhakrishnan et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: DDI2/Nrf1 contributes to the maintenance of basal levels of proteasomes.
source: Previous studies have also reported that DDI2/Nrf1 contributes to the maintenance of basal levels of proteasomes (Chen et al., 2022; Siva et al., 2020; Waku et al., 2020) and that Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the brain (Lee et al., 2011), liver (Lee et al., 2013), and retina Wang et al., 2023; yet, in our experiments, the effects of DDI2 KO on the basal proteasome activity was not significant (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature, but contrasted with the authors' own data.

claim: Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the brain.
source: Previous studies have also reported that DDI2/Nrf1 contributes to the maintenance of basal levels of proteasomes (Chen et al., 2022; Siva et al., 2020; Waku et al., 2020) and that Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the brain (Lee et al., 2011), liver (Lee et al., 2013), and retina Wang et al., 2023; yet, in our experiments, the effects of DDI2 KO on the basal proteasome activity was not significant (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the liver.
source: Previous studies have also reported that DDI2/Nrf1 contributes to the maintenance of basal levels of proteasomes (Chen et al., 2022; Siva et al., 2020; Waku et al., 2020) and that Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the brain (Lee et al., 2011), liver (Lee et al., 2013), and retina Wang et al., 2023; yet, in our experiments, the effects of DDI2 KO on the basal proteasome activity was not significant (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the retina.
source: Previous studies have also reported that DDI2/Nrf1 contributes to the maintenance of basal levels of proteasomes (Chen et al., 2022; Siva et al., 2020; Waku et al., 2020) and that Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the brain (Lee et al., 2011), liver (Lee et al., 2013), and retina Wang et al., 2023; yet, in our experiments, the effects of DDI2 KO on the basal proteasome activity was not significant (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the authors' experiments, the effects of DDI2 KO on the basal proteasome activity was not significant.
source: Previous studies have also reported that DDI2/Nrf1 contributes to the maintenance of basal levels of proteasomes (Chen et al., 2022; Siva et al., 2020; Waku et al., 2020) and that Nrf1 is essential for the basal proteasome expression in the brain (Lee et al., 2011), liver (Lee et al., 2013), and retina Wang et al., 2023; yet, in our experiments, the effects of DDI2 KO on the basal proteasome activity was not significant (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Heavy secretory MM cells, embryonic cells, and certain specific tissues require higher levels of proteasome activity and use the DDI2/Nrf1 pathway to supplement other pathways responsible for proteasome expression.
source: These differences may reflect that heavy secretory MM cells, embryonic cells, and certain specific tissues require higher levels of proteasome activity and use the DDI2/Nrf1 pathway to supplement other pathways responsible for proteasome expression (Motosugi and Murata, 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: Nrf1-dependent proteasome expression is important during cardiac regeneration.
source: Other studies demonstrated the importance of Nrf1-dependent proteasome expression during cardiac regeneration (Cui et al., 2021) and thermogenic adaptation of the brown fat (Bartelt et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Nrf1-dependent proteasome expression is important during thermogenic adaptation of the brown fat.
source: Other studies demonstrated the importance of Nrf1-dependent proteasome expression during cardiac regeneration (Cui et al., 2021) and thermogenic adaptation of the brown fat (Bartelt et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The knockout of DDI2 sensitizes cells to proteasome inhibitors.
source: Several studies found that the knockout of DDI2 sensitizes cells to proteasome inhibitors (Weyburne et al., 2017; Op et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2022; Northrop et al., 2020; Dirac-Svejstrup et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: The present findings raise a possibility that DDI2 desensitizes cells to PI by a different mechanism.
source: Although we confirmed this observation in HAP1 cells (not shown), the present findings raise a possibility that DDI2 desensitizes cells to PI by a different mechanism.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Activation of non-proteasomal Nrf1-dependent oxidative stress response genes may help overcome the deleterious consequences of PI-induced overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS).
source: Activation of non-proteasomal Nrf1-dependent oxidative stress response genes (Ribeiro et al., 2022; Kim et al., 2016) may help overcome the deleterious consequences of PI-induced overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS) (Lipchick et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: The ability of DDI2 to bind and participate in the degradation of large ubiquitin conjugates may help alleviate the stress associated with proteasome inhibition.
source: Alternatively, the ability of DDI2 to bind and participate in the degradation of large ubiquitin conjugates (Dirac-Svejstrup et al., 2020; Collins et al., 2022) may help alleviate the stress associated with proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: DDI2 and proteasome are involved in DNA repair.
source: DDI2 and proteasome are involved in DNA repair (Kottemann et al., 2018; Krogan et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2010; Groisman et al., 2006; Aliyaskarova et al., 2023), and impairment of the proteasome in the absence of DDI2 can lead to excessive spontaneous DNA damage, even without DNA-damaging agents.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Impairment of the proteasome in the absence of DDI2 can lead to excessive spontaneous DNA damage, even without DNA-damaging agents.
source: DDI2 and proteasome are involved in DNA repair (Kottemann et al., 2018; Krogan et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2010; Groisman et al., 2006; Aliyaskarova et al., 2023), and impairment of the proteasome in the absence of DDI2 can lead to excessive spontaneous DNA damage, even without DNA-damaging agents.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the known roles of DDI2 and proteasome.

claim: The study provides strong evidence for a novel pathway responsible for the recovery of proteasome activity in inhibitor-treated cells.
source: In summary, our study provides strong evidence for a novel pathway responsible for the recovery of proteasome activity in inhibitor-treated cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: DDI2 deletion causes embryonic lethality.
source: It should stimulate research on additional biological roles of DDI2, which can explain the embryonic lethality of DDI2 deletion (Siva et al., 2020) and DDI2's role in tumorigenesis (Lei et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: DDI2 has a role in tumorigenesis.
source: It should stimulate research on additional biological roles of DDI2, which can explain the embryonic lethality of DDI2 deletion (Siva et al., 2020) and DDI2's role in tumorigenesis (Lei et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Proteasomes degrade a significant fraction of nascent proteasome subunits within 2–4 hr after synthesis.
source: One study found that proteasomes degrade a significant fraction of nascent proteasome subunits within 2–4 hr after synthesis (McShane et al., 2016), after which the remaining fraction is highly stable (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature and data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: After 2-4 hr, the remaining fraction of nascent proteasome subunits is highly stable.
source: One study found that proteasomes degrade a significant fraction of nascent proteasome subunits within 2–4 hr after synthesis (McShane et al., 2016), after which the remaining fraction is highly stable (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature and data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Nascent proteasome subunits are partitioned between immediate degradation and assembly.
source: We hypothesize that nascent proteasome subunits are partitioned between immediate degradation and assembly, and the inhibition of the proteasome blocks degradation and increases the efficiency of proteasome assembly (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The inhibition of the proteasome blocks degradation of nascent proteasome subunits and increases the efficiency of proteasome assembly.
source: We hypothesize that nascent proteasome subunits are partitioned between immediate degradation and assembly, and the inhibition of the proteasome blocks degradation and increases the efficiency of proteasome assembly (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Increased expression of proteasome assembly chaperone POMP and an increase in proteasome assembly intermediates after treatment with PIs has been previously reported.
source: Increased expression of proteasome assembly chaperone POMP and an increase in proteasome assembly intermediates after treatment with PIs has been previously reported see Figure 6 in Meiners et al., 2003.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: If nascent polypeptides take 1–2 hr to assemble into proteasomes, this model explains translation-independent recovery of proteasome activity in the first hour after the removal of PIs.
source: If nascent polypeptides take 1–2 hr to assemble into proteasomes, this model explains translation-independent recovery of proteasome activity in the first hour after the removal of PIs (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation based on the proposed model.

claim: Partitioning proteasome nascent polypeptides between degradation and assembly allows cells to instantaneously upregulate proteasome biogenesis immediately after proteasome inhibition.
source: Thus, partitioning proteasome nascent polypeptides between degradation and assembly allows cells to instantaneously upregulate proteasome biogenesis immediately after proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the proposed model.

claim: HAP1 cells were cultured in Iscove's medium supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS).
source: HAP1 cells were cultured in Iscove's medium supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS).
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing cell culture conditions.

claim: MDA-MB-231 and SUM149 cells were cultured in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM)/Hams F-12 50/50 Mix supplemented with 5% FBS.
source: MDA-MB-231 and SUM149 cells were cultured in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM)/Hams F-12 50/50 Mix supplemented with 5% FBS.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing cell culture conditions.

claim: HCT-116 cells were cultured in McCoy medium supplemented with 10% FBS.
source: HCT-116 cells were cultured in McCoy medium supplemented with 10% FBS.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing cell culture conditions.

claim: The β5 site is the prime target of Cfz and Btz.
source: We measured inhibition of the proteasome's β5 site, which is the prime target of Cfz and Btz (Kisselev et al., 2012), immediately after the 1 hr treatment, and 12 or 24 hr thereafter (Figure 1c), which is when recovery plateaued (not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Recovery of proteasome activity plateaued at 12 or 24 hr after treatment.
source: We measured inhibition of the proteasome's β5 site, which is the prime target of Cfz and Btz (Kisselev et al., 2012), immediately after the 1 hr treatment, and 12 or 24 hr thereafter (Figure 1c), which is when recovery plateaued (not shown).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Initial inhibition of proteasome was observed at sub-lethal concentrations.
source: Initial inhibition of proteasome was observed at sub-lethal concentrations, and proteasome activity recovered in cells treated with such concentrations.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Proteasome activity recovered in cells treated with sub-lethal concentrations of proteasome inhibitors.
source: Initial inhibition of proteasome was observed at sub-lethal concentrations, and proteasome activity recovered in cells treated with such concentrations.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: VCP inhibitors block Nrf1 processing.
source: The sample in the first lane is wt cells treated with VCP/p97 inhibitor CB-5083 immediately after removal of Btz. VCP inhibitors blocks Nrf1 processing (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014; Sha and Goldberg, 2014; Anderson et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Knockdown of DDI2 by two different highly efficient siRNAs in SUM149 and MDA-MB-231 did not significantly affect the recovery of proteasome activity in cells treated with 100 nM Btz.
source: Next, we knocked down DDI2 by two different highly efficient siRNAs in two PI-sensitive triple-negative breast cancer cell lines, SUM149 and MDA-MB-231 (Figure 1e). Proteasome activity in these cells and their sensitivity to PIs were similar to HAP1 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2). The knockdown did not significantly affect the recovery of proteasome activity in cells treated with 100 nM Btz (Figure 1f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Inactivation of DDI2 by the D252N mutation of the catalytic aspartic acid residue did not block the recovery of activity after pulse treatment of HCT-116 cells with Btz and Cfz.
source: Finally, we found that inactivation of DDI2 by the D252N mutation of the catalytic aspartic acid residue (Koizumi et al., 2016) did not block the recovery of activity after pulse treatment of HCT-116 cells with Btz and Cfz (Figure 1g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: All proteasome mRNAs are actively translated in untreated cells.
source: We found that 90% of proteasomal mRNAs are ribosome or polysome bound in untreated cells (Figure 3b)
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that 90% of proteasomal mRNAs are ribosome or polysome bound, which indicates active translation.
